title: Regular native switching with a unique-visible-window guard
description: Support tta OTHER from a shell already inside tmux by sending switch-client -c CLIENT -t TARGET through tmax. This moves an existing terminal connection; it does not implement terminal attachment/display. Human decision on 2026-10-27: guard by default, reject if more than one client displays the invoking WINDOW. Resolve TMUX_PANE on the selected server, count current viewers across all sessions linking that window, allow exactly one and explicitly pin its client identity. Zero viewers, missing/stale context, failed or incomplete observations also fail. Never use recent activity to guess. The guard is current-visibility policy, not proof of historical input origin. CLI backend enforces the same policy. Start with ordinary existing-session switching, then compose with project/scaffold creation; keep grouped lifecycle queues CLI-owned with explicit client targeting until separately improved. Fresh guard before side effects and revalidation after slow preparation; uncertain native mutation never retries through CLI. Delayed/printed plans must revalidate or explicitly refuse unsupported inside shell emission. No origin-integration dependency. Current home: design/launcher/launch-backends2.gpt6a.md; source homes now session/launcher/{workflow,prepared,plan}.rs and session/runner/{driver,backend,execution}.rs. Latest user direction PAUSES implementation: design/instructions only while adjacent work continues. Provenance: opencode://ses_e9a6011b0ffeBJ4GW5UhFqoHb5.
acceptance_criteria: Implement pure observable guard facts/decision and runtime acquisition without reintroducing I/O into the launcher core. Native default switches the explicit eligible client without a switch-client subprocess; CLI mode uses equivalent guard/target. Two real clients showing the same window (including distinct panes/linked sessions) cause rejection before generator or mutation; one viewer moves only that client; zero/missing/stale/error cases fail. Cover client changes after preparation, slow generators, failed create/switch, delayed shell plans, feature matrix and runner-free/consumer checks. Keep origin uncertainty and remaining native grouped/terminal limits explicit.

title: Name a created session's initial window after the session; --window-name overrides or disables
notes:
Origin: user ask (opencode://ses_e8112b4b3ffexPxCA32QZKg13t) "setting the window title to be the session title if we create the tmux session. ideally there should be a way to set this as an arg."

Decisions confirmed with the user in-session:
- Target is the tmux WINDOW NAME (status-bar label via new-session -n), not a pane title and not the terminal-emulator set-titles string.
- Default posture: ON. When tta creates a session (Project and Create selections), the initial window is named after the session. --window-name=NAME overrides; --window-name=false (or off/none/0) restores today's behavior.

tmux evidence (~/archive/tmux/tmux):
- new-session -n names the initial window AND disables automatic-rename for it (spawn.c: ~224 sets automatic-rename 0 when a name is given). Documented consequence: a named window no longer auto-renames to the running command.
- -n cannot combine with -t ("command or window name given with target", cmd-new-session.c:100). Grouped satellite creation uses -t and shares the group's window list, so satellites never take a window name; scope is exactly "when tta creates the session".
- -n is a tmux format like -s/-c: values need the existing literal_format hash escaping.

Implementation scope:
- session/launcher plan.rs: WindowName enum (Session | Custom(String) | Off) with scaffold::Choice-style parse vocabulary; window_name builder option on launch/prepare_launch (default Session); new-session gains -n <literal_format-ed title>; invalid custom names (empty/control chars) rejected via a new PlanError.
- app/cli: --window-name[=NAME] optional-value require_equals flag (default_missing_value "default"), mapped through WindowName::parse; bare flag = session-name behavior.
- README entry-option table row + automatic-rename consequence note.
- Tests: plan.rs exact-argv unit tests updated for -n; new default/custom/off/escaping/satellite-exclusion tests; CLI print-shell coverage for the three states.

Acceptance: creating a session via tta names its initial window after the session by default; --window-name=NAME renames it; --window-name=false omits -n entirely; grouped satellites and existing-session entry are unchanged; --print-shell reflects all three states.
close_reason: Implemented in tta commit dd4d7498 (ticket commit 7b17bf98). Created sessions name their initial window after the session by default via new-session -n; --window-name=NAME overrides (format-escaped, ./://spaces/# allowed); --window-name=false or bare-absent vocabulary restores the exact pre-feature argv (no -n, automatic-rename untouched). Grouped satellites and existing-session entry unchanged: -n cannot combine with -t and satellites share the group's windows. Launcher WindowName enum + builder option, CLI optional-value require_equals flag, README row/consequences with session provenance (rkt check --okf passes). Verified: workspace nextest 113/113 including live-tmux satellites/acceptance/PTY suites; clippy clean in tta crates; end-to-end on a private /tmp/opencode socket under a real PTY confirmed all three states against the running server, with a plain-tmux control confirming false matches stock behavior. Session: opencode://ses_e8112b4b3ffexPxCA32QZKg13t

title: Default outside entry to independent workspace views
description: Primary outcome: separate terminals entering the same project through ordinary tta independently select their windows while sharing project windows/panes/processes. Human settled the direction on 2026-10-27: independent outside views first; inside native switching uses a unique-visible-window guard, now tracked separately in tta-launch-backends-switching. A future input-origin integration is NOT a prerequisite. Use the already-tested grouped satellite mechanism for existing outside selections; retain cold first creation and a --group=false shared-selection opt-out. CLI resolves its outside default explicitly; SSH entry is also outside. Preserve embedded callers' explicit policy and pure core boundaries. Preserve lifecycle queue ordering and deliberate collision/failure semantics; do not add automatic pruning. Broader canonical group identity/base loss/inside view reuse belongs to follow-up scope under the parent rather than blocking this default. Current implementation instructions: design/launcher/launch-backends2.gpt6a.md. Latest human instruction is DESIGN ONLY while other work is in progress; this ticket is unblocked in design, not implemented. Earlier notes retain investigation history. Provenance: opencode://ses_e9a6011b0ffeBJ4GW5UhFqoHb5.
acceptance_criteria: Ordinary outside tta entry from two real terminals gives distinct grouped sessions sharing windows and panes with independent selected windows in both directions. Cover cold first entry, subsequent existing entry, explicit --group=false, observed tmux version, detach/last-view behavior, shell emission and SSH entry composition. Keep native/CLI outcomes equivalent and preserve queue lifecycle behavior, literal argv/cwd/scaffold contracts. Update CLI help/completion and docs; default policy must be explicit for embedded callers. No input-origin investigation dependency.
notes:
Architectural checkpoint reached, not a completed default/native-switch implementation. Evidence committed in tta 9380e3c5; tmax consumer account in d8bf376d. Pointers: design/launcher/launch-backends1.gpt61sol.md; verification/trials/independent-views/README.md, proof.py, native0.json and cli0.json. Main guide now states current shared default and warns about the inside-switch defect. The preserved trial executes the real tta in TWO REAL PTYs on exclusively owned /tmp/opencode sockets, using version-asserted local tmux 3.7c. Four cases (plain/grouped x native/CLI) reproduced: default terminals share a current window; --group gives separate sessions with shared panes and independent windows. With both views showing the same pane, A enters delayed tta other and B becomes active; B is switched instead of A on both backend selections. Recorded actual native A PID 3345281 -> switched B PID 3345375; CLI A PID 3345285 -> switched B PID 3345373. Identical TMUX/TMUX_PANE/pane tty and tmux source prove that normal shared-pane subprocess context lacks authoritative input-origin identity; a native query of client_name only freezes the recent-activity heuristic. Existing single-client acceptance/launch suites still pass 24/24, exposing the coverage gap. Combined CLI build, generated JSON parsing and rkt documentation/provenance checks pass. No Rust production code/default/API version changed.
Decision needed: (1, recommended) make grouped views default, retain --group=false, add authoritative client-context input/integration from a tmux-owned boundary, native switch-client -c and refuse ambiguity; (2) explicitly accept tmux recent-activity heuristics as a weaker contract; or (3) deliver default independent outside entry separately while leaving the known inside CLI defect pending. Do not silently choose a new knob/integration/error contract. Native attachment still needs real terminal client exec. Native queue compositions remain candidates to test: inside create/switch-explicit-client/keep-last in one queue; outside native create plus satellite-local temporary destroy-unattached=off in one queue, then CLI attach/keep-last. No queue workaround was claimed safe or implemented. Parent/user choice is prerequisite to the next coherent implementation slice. title: Backend-selectable launch execution: native tmax mutations with tmux-client terminal handoff
description:
Origin: user ask "do we use ~/src/tmax or are we shelling out? i'd love a build feature that switches between the two. tempted to make tmax the default." The parent audit (opencode://ses_e9a6011b0ffeBJ4GW5UhFqoHb5, commits dd4d7806/ea852864/9bcb6354) satisfied the LOOKUP half and closed tta-lookup-backends; this ticket holds the remainder so the board shows launch/backend execution still open. It does not claim the closed audit finished native launch.

What exists today (verified by reading current code, opencode://ses_e9a5990dfffeEYjKIU71KHzxZo):
- Lookup alone is backend-selectable. session/launcher/src/backend.rs: Native queries the tmax endpoint directly; Cli runs the same typed Sessions query through a tmux subprocess. app/cli/src/main.rs selects native/cli via Cargo features plus --backend / TTA_BACKEND (CLI > env > native-if-compiled), native default.
- ALL launch mutations and terminal handoff are planned as tmux argv. session/launcher/src/plan.rs builds tta_command Expressions over tmax operation::Invocations (new-session, attach-session, switch-client, set-option destroy-unattached); shell/command executes or renders them; app/cli/src/main.rs execs the tmux client (Handoff::Exec) or renders for eval (--print-shell / --exec-shell).
- Operation matrix (main.rs trace names): existing -> attach-session | switch-client; project -> new-session+attach | new-session-detached+switch-client; create -> scaffold+new-session(+attach | +switch); grouped -> new-grouped-session-detached+attach | +switch-client (detached create, set-option, then client move).

Closed-audit scope (tta-lookup-backends): verified feature selection and native default for session discovery only; fixed 3 scaffold tests that hardcoded the cli backend in native-only builds; documented the boundary in README.md#build-and-install (22/22 native-only, 20/20 cli-only+scaffold, 32/32 combined CLI+PTY). Closure = lookup verification, not native launch.

Remaining outcome: a deliberate backend selection for launch EXECUTION (mutations and handoff), preserving interactive terminal attachment through the real tmux client and unchanged --print-shell emission.

Verified tmax capabilities (~/src/tmax -> ~/src/tmux-interface-control; README and src read this session):
- Native mutation execution exists: endpoint::Tmux::run accepts impl IntoInvocation, implemented for raw operation::Invocation; plan.rs already assembles Invocations with argv boundaries preserved, and typed builders (e.g. NewSession) also run natively.
- Endpoints never spawn a client or start a server. An absent server surfaces as OperationError::ServerConnection; backend.rs already maps NotFound/ConnectionRefused to an empty inventory for lookup.
- Cold server: opt-in server-lifecycle OwnedServer launches `tmux -D` in the foreground at a FRESH explicit socket under a supervisor — private-server ownership, not shared-socket auto-start. Today's CLI plan relies on the exec'd tmux client auto-starting the server; a native create on an absent server fails instead. Cold-start posture is an open decision.
- No interactive terminal client exists in tmax: the process-launching root Tmux was removed, and the persistent Session's control-mode attach is a control client, not a terminal UI. attach-session handoff must remain an exec'd tmux client.

Open questions needing design resolution (design-first is acceptable; do not pre-decide):
- switch-client scope: the CLI command mutates the INVOKING client (tta detects its own context via socket.rs client_mode/$TMUX). A native control connection is a different client; how or whether the user's terminal client can be switched from a control connection is unresolved.
- Atomicity: the grouped flow currently creates + switches + sets destroy-unattached in ONE tmux invocation; splitting mutations (native) from handoff (exec) opens a partial-failure window needing explicit recovery semantics.
- Client-flag mapping: -f config, TMUX_TMPDIR, -L/-S live on the tmux client invocation in the plan; native execution maps the socket via Tmux::new().socket_path/socket_name (socket::Resolved already carries it), but startup-config semantics at server start need a decision.
- Cold-server posture (above) and whether native becomes the default for mutations as it already is for lookup (user leans tmax default).

Coherent possible scope, offered not decided: mirror the SessionLookup seam with a launch-execution seam in session/launcher — plan.rs stays pure assembly; an execution backend chooses native Tmux::run for mutations versus Expression exec, keeping print-shell rendering and terminal handoff on the Expression path.

Implementation homes: session/launcher/src/plan.rs (assembly), session/launcher/src/backend.rs (lookup seam to mirror), shell/command/src/lib.rs (Expression execute/shell), app/cli/src/main.rs (selection, handoff, print-shell), session/launcher/src/socket.rs (socket/client-mode context), README.md#build-and-install.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Design resolved and recorded: backend granularity (Cargo feature vs runtime flag), cold-server posture on absent server, switch-client scope from a control connection, partial-failure semantics for split mutate+handoff, and -f config mapping. 2) A launch-execution seam exists beside SessionLookup with mutation operations runnable natively (Tmux::run over the Invocations plan.rs already builds) and via the CLI path, selected per the decided granularity. 3) Interactive attach/switch terminal handoff still execs the real tmux client; --print-shell/--exec-shell output is unchanged for both selections. 4) Feature-matrix verification on tmux 3.7c: existing/project/create/grouped flows on each backend plus mixed selection, cold-server behavior matching the decided posture, and PTY acceptance coverage mirroring the closed audit's configurations.
notes:
Context ticket written by opencode://ses_e9a5990dfffeEYjKIU71KHzxZo (G subagent) on direction from parent audit opencode://ses_e9a6011b0ffeBJ4GW5UhFqoHb5, which closed tta-lookup-backends as lookup-only. Capability claims verified against ~/src/tmux-interface-control README.md, src/endpoint/mod.rs (run/query signatures), src/server/mod.rs (OwnedServer), src/lib.rs docs, and tta's current backend.rs/plan.rs/main.rs/shell-command. No implementation done here; keep open until the design questions are resolved and an execution seam lands.
Implementation scope selected in opencode://ses_e9a2dad06ffeFURNHXCj1ln0ea (parent opencode://ses_e9a6011b0ffeBJ4GW5UhFqoHb5): take the straight native slice, grouped satellite detached creation only. Keep attach/switch followed by keep-last in one real tmux-client invocation, preserving invoking-client selection, option timing and terminal ownership. Ordinary project/create launches retain CLI creation, cold-start/config behavior and raw Unix startup argv. Add a reusable prepared launch with native/CLI execution selection while preserving the existing launch()->Expression API and unchanged print-shell output. Native errors stop without retry/rollback. Ticket remains open for broader native project creation and switching; no full interactive client or new server supervisor is authorized.
Completed the bounded native-default improvement in opencode://ses_e9a2dad06ffeFURNHXCj1ln0ea (parent opencode://ses_e9a6011b0ffeBJ4GW5UhFqoHb5): tta commit 86f9d87c after preparatory checkpoint a900ac90; tmax commit f7fb3acdf6aba8df72d5f4f2a56eb1816bcf7b69. FINAL SCOPE SUPERSEDES THE EARLIER SATELLITE-SPLIT NOTE: grouped create -> attach/switch -> keep-last stays one CLI queue, because splitting native detached creation allows inherited destroy-unattached to remove the satellite before attachment. Native now creates ordinary project/scaffold sessions detached INSIDE a live selected server when startup argv is UTF-8, then retains exact-target CLI switching of the invoking client. Added prepare_launch()/LaunchPlan/LaunchBackend beside the unchanged launch()->Expression API; native is default when compiled, optional CLI selection remains. Generic tta-command remains tmux-free. Native mutation errors never trigger retry/rollback. Cold or sessionless preflight, outside create+attach, all terminal/client moves, grouped queues and non-UTF8 startup remain deliberate CLI paths; print-shell/exec-shell always emit the complete original CLI plan without executing it. Prefix failure and invalid directory stop before native create; failed creation stops switch; failed handoff may leave creation. Added tmax client_directory(absolute_path) to preserve native identified physical cwd without global chdir; API markers tta 0.2.0 and tmax 0.5.0 with receiving locks refreshed.
Current pointers: README.md#which-operations-use-tmax; design/launcher/launch-backends0.gpt61sol.md (decision, failure policy, rejected split, verification); session/launcher/src/execution.rs; app/cli/tests/launch.rs; library-side /home/rektide/src/tmux-interface-control/doc/consumer/tta.md.
Verification: system tmux was discovered to be 3.8, so built and version-asserted a private 3.7c binary from the local archive tag and repeated the full feature matrix with it first on PATH. Pinned 3.7c workspace nextest: default native+scaffold 110/110, CLI-only 84/84, combined 122/122. System 3.8 also passed 110/84/122 configurations, and CLI-only with explicit scaffold features passed 24/24 focused CLI/launch/scaffold/PTY checks. Combined and CLI-only clippy --all-targets --no-deps -D warnings passed; formatting and workspace doctests passed; rkt OKF/link/provenance checks passed. Library isolated endpoint tests 6/6 and streams locked offline compile passed. Adjacent tmax materialize compile remains blocked by its existing unhandled Kubeless PublicationReport::Enqueued; only receiving locks were refreshed, no unrelated materialize implementation changed. All sockets private under /tmp/opencode.
Ticket deliberately remains OPEN for broader native switch-client identity, queue-preserving grouped mutation and raw-byte startup capabilities; this is not a full native terminal client or all-launch migration. The user-authorized straightforward default-native creation slice is complete.
2026-10-23 human clarified the primary outcome: each tta-entered terminal independently chooses its window over shared project windows/processes, while advancing native tmax switching/attachment preparation. Added linked child tta-launch-backends-independent-views (blocked at explicit user/parent targeting-contract choice). Investigation/evidence in tta 9380e3c5 and tmax consumer-account commit d8bf376d. Pointers: design/launcher/launch-backends1.gpt61sol.md and verification/trials/independent-views/README.md. Two real PTYs on pinned tmux 3.7c confirm grouping provides exactly the requested window independence, whereas plain current default shares the session selection. Also reproduced an existing wrong-client switch on BOTH backend selections: A invokes delayed tta other, B becomes active, and B moves instead. Shared-pane TMUX, TMUX_PANE and tty are identical; client_name lookup does not prove origin. This is already a CLI defect, so merely native-switching its inferred client would not be robust. Existing acceptance/launch tests remain green 24/24; the preserved four-case trial exposes the uncovered ambiguity. Recommended next contract: grouped default with --group=false escape, authoritative client context from a boundary that knows the actual tmux client, explicit native -c targeting and ambiguity refusal. Parent should select that versus deliberately accepting weaker activity heuristics or splitting outside-default delivery first. No new production defaults/native-switch APIs were silently implemented. Broader ticket remains OPEN; real interactive attachment still requires tmux client exec. Native grouped preparation/queue options are recorded as unverified candidates, not dismissed as fundamentally impossible or claimed implemented. Session opencode://ses_e9a2dad06ffeFURNHXCj1ln0ea; parent opencode://ses_e9a6011b0ffeBJ4GW5UhFqoHb5.
2026-10-27 human direction and design-only checkpoint, opencode://ses_e9a6011b0ffeBJ4GW5UhFqoHb5: independent outside views are chosen; regular inside switching should use native tmax with default rejection unless exactly one client displays the invoking WINDOW. This is a visibility guard, not historical input-origin proof. notes:

Decisions recorded 2026-10-22:
- Trigger: unambiguous miss only (no session, no immediate directory under root, no candidates). Ambiguity still stops; existing sessions still win.
- Adapter crates: each scaffolding system is its own crate under scaffold/ behind app/cli cargo features. v1: scaffold/rekon wraps the external rekon script (program rekon, one arg: project name, PATH lookup). title: Explore input-origin assistance for ambiguous inside-tmux invocations
description: Investigate whether additional information can let tta run usefully when multiple clients display the invoking window, beyond the chosen default visibility guard. Human request: keep possible assistance as tentative leads, not an authoritative stance or a selected solution. Shared pane shells inherit identical TMUX/TMUX_PANE/tty; the preserved delayed-command trial shows recent activity can select the wrong terminal. Possible leads: a tmux binding/command prompt that knows its client, a per-invocation client hint, or an embedding application that owns a terminal connection. Determine whether each establishes invocation origin or merely names a requested target, and how to validate lifetime/server membership, expiry and reuse. Activity timestamps, environment variables and a query of client_name are not proven origin evidence. Do not assume an always-subscribed monitor or require integration before the guarded version can ship. Compare workflow cost, uncertainty and failures; recommend only after evidence. Context: design/launcher/launch-backends2.gpt6a.md#input-origin-investigation-leads-not-commitments and verification/trials/independent-views/. Related implementation ticket: tta-launch-backends-switching. No implementation authorized in this design pass. Provenance: opencode://ses_e9a6011b0ffeBJ4GW5UhFqoHb5.
acceptance_criteria: Explain candidate information sources with actual guarantees and counterexamples for shared panes, delayed commands, client detach/reuse, and embedded callers. Distinguish authoritative context if demonstrable, advisory hints and explicit user target selection. Describe a possible usable invocation contract and how it could avoid the default ambiguity rejection, without silently disabling the guard or claiming unverified origin certainty. Findings may conclude no lightweight inference is available. No dependency blocking independent views or regular guarded native switching.

title: Versioned structured carrier so stale remote tta degrades gracefully
Forward the remote tmux socket over ssh for native backend targeting
notes:
Design context: /design/launcher/remote0.glm53max.md direction B (verified 2026-10-27: tmux protocol survives socket relaying — socat UNIX-LISTEN→UNIX-CONNECT trial served ls and list-panes identically; ssh -L unix forwarding is the same relay over the transport, documented but not yet exercised). Sibling exploration: tta-launch-backends-remote-target.

Scope: establish an ssh -N -L <local.sock>:<remote.sock> side channel so SessionLookup::Native and native execution operate against a remote server through a local endpoint, without requiring any tta binary on the target host.

Considerations already identified: cold start still needs one remote exec (no server, no socket to forward); the tmux protocol has no authentication — the local forwarded endpoint grants full remote server control, so endpoint placement/permissions need an explicit stance; forward lifecycle ownership (ControlMaster, cleanup on failure); mosh cannot forward — hybrid per-state placement (attach over mosh's remote client, structured ops over the ssh forward) or ssh-only degradation must be chosen explicitly; local-client attach through the forward is possible but carries client/server version skew.

Acceptance: native lookup and mutation work against a remote server via the forwarded endpoint; forward lifecycle is owned start-to-stop with no leak on failure paths; the security stance is documented; mosh behavior is a deliberate choice, not an accident; generated carriers keep quoting '=$name' targets for zsh.
